content.text: (gallstone ileus, FB, intussusception)	  ▪︎i.e., bowel ischemia, perforation, red flags
: only part of lumen is occluded,
allowing some passage of intraluminal contents
no passage of intraluminal content distal to obstruction
both proximal & distal ends of obstructed loop closed
(e.g., volvulus, obstructed inguinal hernia); can rapidly lead to ischemia & perforation ⇢ surgery necessary
adenocarcinoma > scarring secondary to diverticulitis > volvulus
•major factor in clinical course of LBO is
ileocecal valve does NOT allow reflux to occur
impaired capillary circulation, mucosal ischemia, bacterial translocation
torsion of bowel on its axis
•torsion of mesenteric vascular pedicle ⇢ occlusion/thrombosis of mesenteric vessels ⇢ bowel
d/t intense intestinal muscular contraction (“peristaltic rush”)
, may be absent if ileocecal valve prevents reflux
SCr indicative of hypovolemia w/ prerenal failure
dilated bowel loops w/ air-fluid levels in ladder-like appearance
•dilated small bowel loops w/ multiple air-fluid levels
•NPO, IV fluids, foley to monitor urine output
: ileocecal resection or R colectomy w/ ileocolic anastomosis
sigmoidoscopy w/ rectal tube insertion for
